name: RAC-alpha serine/threonine-protein kinase
function_description: Serine/threonine-protein kinase that regulates many processes including metabolism, proliferation, cell survival, growth and angiogenesis. Mediates the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.

name: Epidermal growth factor receptor
function_description: Receptor tyrosine kinase that binds epidermal growth factor and activates downstream signaling cascades to convert extracellular signals to cellular responses.

go_terms.term: receptor signaling protein tyrosine kinase activity
epidermal growth factor receptor signaling pathway

name: Proto-oncogene tyrosine-protein kinase Src
function_description: Non-receptor tyrosine kinase that plays a role in the regulation of cell growth, differentiation, migration, and immune response. Involved in signaling pathways triggered by receptor tyrosine kinases.

go_terms.term: transmembrane receptor protein tyrosine kinase signaling pathway

name: Tyrosine-protein kinase ABL1
function_description: Non-receptor tyrosine kinase involved in cell differentiation, cell division, cell adhesion, and stress response. The BCR-ABL fusion protein is the hallmark of chronic myeloid leukemia.

name: Serine/threonine-protein kinase B-raf
function_description: Serine/threonine-protein kinase that plays a role in regulating the MAP kinase/ERK signaling pathway affecting cell division, differentiation, and secretion.

name: Dual specificity mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase 1
function_description: Dual specificity kinase that activates ERK1 and ERK2 MAP kinases. Essential component of the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK signal transduction pathway.

name: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4
function_description: Serine/threonine-protein kinase involved in the control of the cell cycle G1/S transition. Phosphorylates and inhibits members of the retinoblastoma protein family.

go_terms.term: G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle

name: Cyclin-dependent kinase 6
function_description: Serine/threonine-protein kinase involved in cell cycle regulation. Partners with D-type cyclins to phosphorylate the retinoblastoma protein.

go_terms.term: G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle

name: Tyrosine-protein kinase JAK2
function_description: Non-receptor tyrosine kinase involved in cytokine receptor signaling. Mediates signaling through the JAK-STAT pathway for cell proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis.

name: Receptor tyrosine-protein kinase erbB-2
function_description: Receptor tyrosine kinase that is part of the EGFR family. Lacks a known ligand but heterodimerizes with other EGFR family members to activate downstream signaling.

go_terms.term: receptor signaling protein tyrosine kinase activity
transmembrane receptor protein tyrosine kinase signaling pathway

name: GTPase KRas
function_description: Small GTPase that acts as a molecular switch in cell signaling. Cycles between active GTP-bound and inactive GDP-bound forms to regulate cell growth, differentiation, and survival.

name: GTPase NRas
function_description: Small GTPase involved in signal transduction. Mutations are found in various cancers, particularly melanoma and acute myeloid leukemia.

name: Phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate 3-kinase catalytic subunit alpha isoform
function_description: Catalytic subunit of PI3K that phosphorylates phosphatidylinositol lipids. Activates AKT signaling to regulate cell growth, survival, and metabolism.

name: Serine/threonine-protein kinase mTOR
function_description: Central regulator of cell growth and metabolism. Integrates signals from growth factors, nutrients, and energy status to control protein synthesis and autophagy.

name: Phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate 3-phosphatase and dual-specificity protein phosphatase PTEN
function_description: Tumor suppressor that antagonizes the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway by dephosphorylating PIP3. Loss of PTEN function leads to uncontrolled cell growth.

name: Retinoblastoma-associated protein
function_description: Key regulator of the cell cycle that acts as a tumor suppressor. In its hypophosphorylated form, it binds E2F transcription factors to prevent G1/S transition.

go_terms.term: G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle

name: Cellular tumor antigen p53
function_description: Tumor suppressor that responds to diverse cellular stresses by regulating expression of target genes involved in cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, senescence, and DNA repair.

name: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase Mdm2
function_description: E3 ubiquitin ligase that targets tumor suppressor p53 for proteasomal degradation. Acts as a key negative regulator of p53 in a feedback loop.

name: Catenin beta-1
function_description: Key downstream component of the Wnt signaling pathway. Functions as both a structural component of cell-cell adhesion junctions and a transcriptional co-activator.

name: Neurogenic locus notch homolog protein 1
function_description: Transmembrane receptor that regulates cell fate decisions during development. Upon ligand binding, the intracellular domain is cleaved and translocates to the nucleus to activate transcription.

name: Collagen alpha-1(I) chain
function_description: Major structural protein of bone, skin, tendon, and other connective tissues. Forms a triple helix with two alpha-1 and one alpha-2 chains.

name: Collagen alpha-1(II) chain
function_description: Major structural component of cartilage. Essential for the normal development of bones and other connective tissues.

name: Fibronectin
function_description: Extracellular matrix glycoprotein that binds integrins, collagen, fibrin, and heparan sulfate. Plays a major role in cell adhesion, migration, and wound healing.

name: Prelamin-A/C
function_description: Type V intermediate filament protein that forms the nuclear lamina. Provides structural support for the nucleus and plays roles in gene regulation and chromatin organization.

name: Vimentin
function_description: Type III intermediate filament protein expressed in mesenchymal cells. Plays a role in cell attachment, migration, and signaling. A marker of epithelial-mesenchymal transition.

name: Tubulin alpha-1B chain
function_description: Major constituent of microtubules. Tubulin alpha/beta heterodimers polymerize to form microtubules essential for cell division, intracellular transport, and cell shape.

name: Actin, alpha skeletal muscle
function_description: Major component of the thin filaments in skeletal muscle sarcomeres. Essential for muscle contraction and force generation.

name: Desmin
function_description: Type III intermediate filament protein expressed in muscle cells. Maintains the structural and mechanical integrity of myofibrils by connecting them at the Z-disc.

name: Keratin, type I cytoskeletal 18
function_description: Type I intermediate filament chain expressed in simple epithelia. Partners with KRT8 to form the major intermediate filament network in epithelial cells of internal organs.

name: Myosin-7
function_description: Heavy chain of cardiac beta-myosin. Functions as the major contractile protein in the heart, converting chemical energy into mechanical force for cardiac contraction.

name: Sodium-dependent dopamine transporter
function_description: Transports dopamine from the synaptic cleft back into presynaptic neurons. Key regulator of dopaminergic neurotransmission and primary target for psychostimulants.

name: Sodium-dependent serotonin transporter
function_description: Transports serotonin from the synaptic cleft back into presynaptic neurons. Primary target for selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) used to treat depression.

name: Multidrug resistance protein 1
function_description: ATP-dependent efflux pump that transports various hydrophobic compounds out of cells. Plays a major role in multidrug resistance in cancer cells.

name: ATP-binding cassette sub-family G member 2
function_description: ABC half-transporter that functions as a drug efflux pump. Transports various substrates including uric acid, drugs, and dietary toxins across cell membranes.

name: Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator
function_description: cAMP-regulated chloride channel that also regulates other ion channels. Mutations cause cystic fibrosis, the most common lethal genetic disease in Caucasian populations.

diseases.name: Congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens

name: Copper-transporting ATPase 2
function_description: Copper-transporting P-type ATPase that is essential for copper homeostasis. Delivers copper to ceruloplasmin in the secretory pathway and excretes excess copper into bile.

name: Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 1
function_description: Facilitative glucose transporter responsible for constitutive glucose uptake. Major glucose transporter in the blood-brain barrier and erythrocytes.

name: Solute carrier family 12 member 1
function_description: Sodium-potassium-chloride co-transporter expressed in the kidney thick ascending limb. Mediates reabsorption of sodium, potassium, and chloride from urine.

name: Solute carrier family 22 member 1
function_description: Organic cation transporter expressed primarily in the liver. Mediates hepatic uptake of various organic cations including metformin and other drugs.

name: ATP-sensitive inward rectifier potassium channel 11
function_description: Inward-rectifier potassium channel that forms the pore of the ATP-sensitive potassium channel in pancreatic beta cells. Couples cell metabolism to electrical activity for insulin secretion.

name: Breast cancer type 1 susceptibility protein
function_description: E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that plays a central role in DNA repair through the homologous recombination pathway. Also involved in transcriptional regulation and cell cycle checkpoint control.

name: Breast cancer type 2 susceptibility protein
function_description: Mediator of homologous recombination DNA repair. Loads RAD51 onto single-stranded DNA to initiate strand invasion and repair of double-strand breaks.

go_terms.term: double-strand break repair via homologous recombination

name: Serine-protein kinase ATM
function_description: Serine/threonine-protein kinase that is recruited to DNA double-strand breaks. Activates checkpoint signaling upon DNA damage, acting as a DNA damage sensor.

go_terms.term: cellular response to DNA damage stimulus

name: Serine/threonine-protein kinase ATR
function_description: Serine/threonine-protein kinase that acts as a DNA damage sensor. Activated by single-stranded DNA regions and stalled replication forks to initiate checkpoint signaling.

name: DNA mismatch repair protein Mlh1
function_description: Key component of the DNA mismatch repair system. Partners with PMS2 to form the MutL-alpha heterodimer that corrects base-base mismatches and insertion/deletion loops.

name: DNA mismatch repair protein Msh2
function_description: Component of the post-replicative DNA mismatch repair system. Heterodimerizes with MSH6 to form MutS-alpha, which recognizes single base mismatches and short insertion/deletion loops.

name: DNA repair protein RAD51 homolog 1
function_description: Recombinase that catalyzes strand transfer between a broken DNA molecule and its homologous template. Essential for homologous recombination repair of DNA double-strand breaks.

go_terms.term: double-strand break repair via homologous recombination

name: Poly [ADP-ribose] polymerase 1
function_description: Chromatin-associated enzyme that detects DNA strand breaks and catalyzes poly(ADP-ribosyl)ation of target proteins. Acts as a first responder to DNA damage to initiate repair.

name: Tumor suppressor p53-binding protein 1
function_description: DNA damage response protein that promotes non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) repair. Rapidly recruited to sites of DNA double-strand breaks where it forms nuclear foci.

name: Serine/threonine-protein kinase Chk2
function_description: Serine/threonine-protein kinase required for checkpoint-mediated cell cycle arrest and DNA repair in response to double-strand breaks. Activated by ATM phosphorylation.
